The potential difference Vout across the fixed resistor is 4.50 V when the thermistor is at a
temperature of 20.0 °C.
What is Vout when the thermistor is at a temperature of 50.0 °C?

hints: Notice $V_{out}$ is the p.d. across the lower $12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ fixed resistor in series with the thermistor, so the two resistances share the battery p.d.
Recall the potential divider rule $V = E \times R/(R+r)$ for this series loop with negligible internal resistance, where $R = 12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$.

First use the $20.0^{\circ}\text{C}$ data where both resistances are $12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ and $V_{out} = 4.50 \text{ V}$ to find the battery e.m.f., then keep that e.m.f. fixed and apply the divider again with $5.00 \text{ k}\Omega$.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit as a series potential divider: battery e.m.f. $E$ is shared between $R_{th}$ on top and $R = 12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ below, with $V_{out}$ across $R$.
At $20.0^{\circ}\text{C}$, $R_{th} = 12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ and $R = 12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$, so the total is $24.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ and the divider gives $V_{out} = E \times 12.0/24.0$.
Substitute $V_{out} = 4.50 \text{ V}$ to find $E = 4.50 \times 24.0/12.0 = 9.00 \text{ V}$, which stays constant because internal resistance is negligible.
At $50.0^{\circ}\text{C}$, $R_{th} = 5.00 \text{ k}\Omega$, so total resistance is $5.00 + 12.0 = 17.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ and $V_{out} = E \times 12.0/17.0$.
Calculate $V_{out} = 9.00 \times 12.0/17.0 = 108/17 = 6.35 \text{ V}$ with unit $\text{V}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is the p.d. across the $5.00 \text{ k}\Omega$ thermistor at $50.0^{\circ}\text{C}$, not $V_{out}$ across the fixed $12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ resistor.

B.explanation: This value is too low because $V_{out}$ must increase when thermistor resistance falls from $12.0 \text{ k}\Omega$ to $5.00 \text{ k}\Omega$.

C.explanation: With battery e.m.f. $9.00 \text{ V}$, $V_{out} = 9.00 \times 12.0/(5.00+12.0) = 6.35 \text{ V}$ across the fixed resistor.

D.explanation: This multiplies $4.50 \text{ V}$ by $12.0/5.00$ and ignores that the total series resistance also changes, so the battery p.d. is not shared in that simple ratio.
